Two sorting bins stand beside paths, planting, or brick fencing.<br>• S07-B-01: a clean stainless-steel recyclables/other-waste bin has a closed lid and no spillage, with only leaves nearby.<br>• S07-B-03: a similar bin has black bags reaching and overflowing its recyclables opening, orange sticker residue, and small ground debris, before a red-brick wall and wooden fence. Neither site has accumulated waste or obvious scattered bags, cardboard, or foam containers. |
| Regulatory basis | • Containers should be clean, intact, non-overflowing, and unobstructed at openings. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 15.<br>• Regular collection should prevent accumulation and spillage, with increased service near busy stations. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 22.<br>• Property or sanitation managers should inspect, maintain, collect, and log collection times, frequency, and quantities. Technical Specification for Municipal Solid Waste Collection, Transport, and Treatment (CJJ/T 275-2017), Section 4.3.2.<br>• Littering or materials storage around bins and failure to clear overflow are prohibited. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 29.<br>• Delayed collection causing overflow or impaired appearance may incur warnings or fines, with suspension in serious cases where persuasion fails or uncorrected incidents recur. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 34. |
| Severity | **Moderate.** One bin overflows without litter or accumulation, but its busy station location creates sanitation and appearance risks requiring prompt action. |
| Impact assessment | Visible impacts: waste at the S07-B-03 opening may cause insects or odors and impair pedestrians. Possible short-term impacts: delays may allow ground spillage and secondary pollution, with complaints or sanitation incidents during peaks. |
| Potential causes | - **Possible cause 1:** excessive collection intervals at a busy high-generation site; verify logs or vehicle visits.<br>- **Possible cause 2:** opening design or capacity inadequacy; the recyclables opening alone overflows. Compare similar bins and category-specific demand.<br>- **Possible cause 3:** missed inspection or cleaning, suggested by sticker residue and debris; verify logs or surveillance. |
| Long-term effects | If persistent or recurrent, prolonged overflow may spill and scatter waste, breed vectors and pathogens, weaken sorting participation, impair the city's civic image, and prompt penalties or media exposure. |
| Recommendations | - **Immediate actions:** empty S07-B-03, assess damage or capacity, clear debris, close the lid, and clean the container.<br>- **Long-term measures:** (1) collect at least twice daily, with extra peak visits; (2) assess capacity and add larger bins or locations; (3) inspect and log collections and address problems immediately; (4) display collection schedules for transparency and public supervision. |
| Priority | **Medium.** One overflow in a busy station area poses sanitation and appearance risks and may worsen quickly. Complete collection and rectification within 24 hours; no public safety emergency is present. |
